label: Feedback loop
summary: A feedback loop, in Maaike's work, is the structured process of receiving, examining, and acting on feedback to improve content quality. It is not treated as a one-off correction but as a repeatable cycle with distinct checks. The content quality audit is her concrete tool for running this loop.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike uses a 5-point checklist to work through feedback systematically, covering facts, audience fit, stakeholder expectations, quality trade-offs, and whether the feedback itself is actually valid. She frames the loop as something that works best when paired with a meeting with the feedback-giver, so she can understand both the person and the topic properly. Importantly, she includes a step that most writers skip: questioning whether the feedback deserves to be acted on at all, based on who gave it and why.
open_questions: The passage on evaluating feedback quality is cut off mid-example, so it is unclear how Maaike recommends handling feedback from stakeholders who are not qualified but still have authority.
The checklist mentions working with audience members at every phase of content design, but how that integrates with the feedback loop in practice is not fully explained.
